latest_final: The student was excellent at individual tests and exams, so their personal work would normally pass easily. This course, however, included a group project weighted heavily enough to determine the course outcome. The student's groupmate — the classmate assigned to the group — did absolutely nothing on the project. Because the project was graded as a single shared group grade rather than by individual contribution, the classmate's total non-contribution dragged the shared project grade down to a failing level. That failing group grade was then applied to the student's course grade, and because the project carried enough weight, it alone pulled the student's overall average below passing. So the smart student who always passes failed the course not through any error, cheating, illness, mistake, or unfair instructor action, but because a non-contributing classmate's zero in a shared group project sank the shared grade to which the student was bound.
